disclaimer.no_attorney_client: Using this app does not make us your lawyers and does not create an attorney–client relationship.
disclaimer.not_filing_service: We do not file anything with any court. You print, sign, and file the paperwork yourself.
disclaimer.not_law_firm_long: This app is a paperwork preparation tool, not a law firm. It does not provide legal advice, and using it does not create an attorney–client relationship. Divorce law and court forms change: verify everything you generate here against your county clerk's current requirements before filing. If your situation is complicated in any way, talk to a licensed attorney in your state.
disclaimer.not_law_firm_short: We are not a law firm. This app prepares paperwork — it does not provide legal advice.
disclaimer.not_legal_advice: Nothing in this app is legal advice. For advice about your specific situation, consult a licensed attorney.

eligibility.heading: Is this for you? Answer honestly.
eligibility.no_redirect: If you answered no to any question, this tool is not built for your situation. See below.
eligibility.q_agree: Do you and your spouse agree on every part of the divorce — property, debts, and the divorce itself?
eligibility.q_children: Do you have any minor children together (including adopted children or a child on the way)?
eligibility.q_cooperate: Will your spouse cooperate — review the paperwork and sign where needed?
eligibility.q_property_divided: Have you already divided your property and debts between yourselves?
eligibility.q_residency_ok: Has at least one of you lived in Oklahoma for the last 6 months, and in the county where you'll file for the last 30 days?
eligibility.q_residency_tx: Has at least one of you lived in Texas for the last 6 months, and in the county where you'll file for the last 90 days?
eligibility.q_simple: Is your situation simple — no domestic violence, no protective orders, no hidden assets?
eligibility.yes_continue: If you answered yes to every question above, you can continue.

not_for.attorney_line: If any of the above sounds like you, talk to a licensed family-law attorney in your state instead. This tool can't help you safely.
not_for.children: You have minor children together. Texas and Oklahoma handle custody and support under different rules and longer waiting periods — get a lawyer.
not_for.complex_assets: You have retirement accounts to split (QDRO), a business, or complicated debts.
not_for.contested: You and your spouse disagree on anything — property, debts, or the divorce itself.
not_for.heading: This tool is NOT for you if…
not_for.name_change_note: If either of you wants to change your name as part of the divorce, confirm the procedure with your county clerk — it varies.
not_for.uncooperative_spouse: Your spouse won't review and sign the paperwork, or you can't locate them.
not_for.violence: There is domestic violence, a protective order, or you feel unsafe. Call the National Domestic Violence Hotline: 1-800-799-7233.

pricing.checkout_closed: Checkout is open in test mode only — no real money moves. Walk through the questionnaire and try the $30 test checkout; the card is simulated.
pricing.fees_separate: Court filing fees are separate and are paid to the court, not to us. In Texas, filing fees are set by each county (for example, Harris County charges $350 for a divorce with no children). In Oklahoma, the state flat fee is $183, but counties add surcharges (for example, Canadian County lists $255.89). Always confirm the exact fee with your county clerk.
pricing.no_refund_placeholder: Test mode: no real payment is taken, so there is nothing to refund. Our refund policy for live checkout will be published before real payments open.
pricing.price_line: $30 fixed — one time. That's our price for preparing your paperwork.

print_banner.organizer: This page is an organizer and worksheet — not a court form. Court requirements change: verify this paperwork against your county clerk's current instructions before you file.
print_banner.signatures: Both spouses must sign where indicated. Unsigned paperwork will be rejected.
print_banner.verify_clerk: Before filing, confirm with your county clerk: the exact filing fee, which forms they require, and who must appear in court.

privacy.honest: No accounts, no uploads. Everything you enter is prepared locally in your browser and never leaves your device.
privacy.orders_future: When checkout opens, the only thing we will ever store is order transaction history — never the contents of your forms.

waiting_periods.ok: Oklahoma: after you file, you must wait at least 10 days before a judge can grant the divorce (no minor children).
waiting_periods.tx: Texas: after you file, you must wait at least 60 days before a judge can grant the divorce.
